subject: Short-term commitment smoothing and autoscale exception
messages:
From: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.example.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.example.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.example.com>, markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.example.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>, ops@orchidretail.com
Date: Fri, 27 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Short-term commitment smoothing and autoscale exception

Team —

Quick summary: Orchid Retail (pilot customer) is asking for a temporary smoothing of their committed GPU pool over the next 6 weeks while they shift traffic between regions. They signed a Dedicated reservation but have a bumpy traffic pattern that will spike for a few daytime hours in US-west and drop overnight. They want two things: (1) a short-term flexibility window to borrow extra slots during their peak hours without breaking the monthly commit, and (2) an autoscale policy exception to allow higher burst targets for the pilot store checkout flow.

Asking:
- Ops/Capacity (Jonas/Markus): can we model a 6-week smoothing plan that keeps aggregate committed capacity unchanged but allows hourly headroom (+25% for 8 hours/day) and compensates overnight? We need feasibility, risk, and P0/P1 failure modes.
- Product (Kimberly/Laura): what guardrails do we want in-platform (billing ramps/alerting/rollback) if we grant this exception? Also, confirm whether we treat this under the Dedicated SLA or as a pilot carveout.
- Sales (Marissa): please confirm commercial acceptability (does this require a formal amendment or can we use a one-off addendum).

I attached a quick workbook with proposed smoothing scenarios and a draft ops runbook. If this looks operationally safe, I want to include it in the next Monday capacity triage and convert to an INF ticket for implementation.

Thanks —
Neha
Neha Kapoor
Sr. Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: commit-smoothing-v1.xlsx (Excel)] [Attachment: ops-runbook-draft.md (Markdown)]
From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.example.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.example.com>, markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.example.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.example.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>, ops@orchidretail.com
Date: Fri, 27 May 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Short-term commitment smoothing and autoscale exception

Neha —

Thanks for the write-up and the workbook; skimmed it and the scenarios are helpful. High-level comments from Capacity: we can support a 6-week smoothing window as long as: (a) total committed GPU-hours per billing period don't decrease, (b) we set a conservative hard cap on per-customer burst (I would suggest +20% initially, but +25% might be OK if we pair with preemptible fallback), and (c) we have automated rollback thresholds tied to cluster saturation and latency SLOs.

Questions before we commit:
- Is Orchid okay with scheduled peak windows (e.g., 14:00–22:00 PT) rather than fully-dynamic bursts? That simplifies routing and reduces preemption risk.
- Do we require manual approval for each day the burst is used, or can it be self-serve for the 6-week window with logging for audits?
- Can Product provide the billing signal we need to compute true 30-day committed usage vs burst consumption?

I'll run a quick sim against recent utilization curves (need the last 30 days from Orchid) and drop results into the Jira ticket. If we go forward, we should scope a short canary (3 days) before opening the full 6 weeks.

— Jonas
Jonas Weber
Capacity & Reliability
From: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.example.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.example.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.example.com>, markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.example.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>, ops@orchidretail.com
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Short-term commitment smoothing and autoscale exception

Thanks Jonas — answers inline and added the Orchid 30-day telemetry link to the Drive.

- Scheduled windows: Orchid prefers scheduled windows (14:00–22:00 PT local). They want predictability for their peak promotions. That should work.
- Approval model: they want self-serve within the 6-week window (no manual approval each day), but with daily email summaries and an API call we can require before the first burst each day to confirm. That gives them programmatic control and us an audit hook.
- Billing signal: Product — can we expose a per-customer committed usage metric in the Console and an API endpoint for burst consumption? If not, Orchid insists on a manual reconciliation statement at month-end.

I've updated the workbook with the scheduled-window plan and a proposed canary (3 days, progressive ramp). See Drive: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/commit-smoothing

We need Product + Capacity to sign off by EOD Wednesday (2 June) to make Monday triage. If we miss that, Orchid wants us to escalate.

Neha

All —

After syncing with Product and Finance: Product is comfortable shipping an in-console guardrail and an API-based burst toggle for the pilot. Conditions:

1) Burst must be tied to a scheduled window (14:00–22:00 PT) and a per-customer daily cap.
2) Console will show a "Burst in effect" flag and a one-click rollback that immediately disables the policy.
3) Billing: Finance agrees to handle reconciliation but wants a short amendment (one paragraph) that documents the 6-week smoothing window and the canary. No change to the underlying monthly committed spend — bursts will be credited back if needed at month-end. Marissa, please confirm the amendment language is acceptable and whether legal needs to sign.

Operationally, Capacity should implement the canary and the health checks Jonas suggested. Ops (Orchid) — we'll need a schedule and the 30-day telemetry link Jonas requested. Once Capacity posts the simulation and the canary plan in INF-9821, Product will prepare a short Console UX for the toggle and the alerting thresholds.

Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Head of Product, Redwood Inference
